items.title: Measured intent accuracy
items.question: How often does Jev pick the same intent as a person?
items.sample: 50 reviews. One person wrote every label before seeing any model output.
items.truth: The original human labels, scored with the course checker's score_gold. Three separate Jev runs per prompt.
items.finding: Jev is strong on praise and complaint. It finds only 56–67% of the reviews a person called unclear. It predicted cancellation once in every run, although the person labelled none.
limits: Line A pipeline. Its prompt v2 ports the topic wording of the production jev-rubric-v2, so the label configuration is close to, but not byte-identical with, the dashboard database. This file holds aggregates only: no review IDs, review texts or human labels.
50 reviews is a small sample: request has 3 cases, so one review moves its score by 33 points.
One person labelled the set. There is no second labeller to measure human agreement.

items.title: Prompt benchmark: rubric v1 against v2
items.question: Does the revised labelling prompt change the labels, and what does it cost?
items.sample: 100 reviews from the course cost sample, labelled twice with the same model
items.truth: None. This compares two prompts with each other. It shows how much labels move, not which prompt is right.
items.decision: v2 is the production prompt. It moved 32 of 100 topics and almost no severities, so the ranking input is stable across the prompt change.
limits: Usage-derived cost is not independently reconciled with account credit debit.
Summed request durations are not end-to-end wall time.
The v2 launcher's cross-process monotonic clock produced an invalid negative wall time.
Saved evidence is compatible only where all four labels match; it was not copied into v2.
Topic changes and manual development judgments are not gold accuracy measurements.

items.title: Labelling runs: cost, speed and reliability
items.question: Can the labelling step run cheaply, without errors, and be replayed without new model calls?
items.sample: Pilot: 100 reviews (prompt v1). Checkpoint: 500 reviews (prompt v2).
items.truth: Structural checks only: schema, source identity and exact evidence quotes. Not label accuracy.

gaps.label: Historical error count unavailable
gaps.detail: The checkpoint report did not save schema or identity-error counts. Final valid outputs cannot recover failed attempts; the missing cell stays unknown.

rows.label: Schema or identity errors
rows.note: The checkpoint report does not count this field.

rows.label: Label stage time
rows.note: Pilot: summed request time. Checkpoint: measured wall time.

limits: Cost is computed from returned usage at the published rate; the account debit was not independently checked.
Summed request time is not total wall time. The runner did not persist cold wall time.
Labels and evidence have not been verified against human answers; structural checks do not establish semantic accuracy.
The checkpoint report has no historical schema-error count. Accepted final outputs do not prove that count was zero.

items.sample: Estimate: the first 100,000 rows, before any model call. Measured: every call of the 110,000-row selection.
items.truth: Measured charges are usage-derived from the saved call ledger in the grading release.

gaps.label: Billing unresolved
gaps.detail: 46 calls have unknown charges. Known charges are not the final bill; full reservations remain held.

gaps.label: Historical forecast gaps
gaps.detail: Evidence-cost and call-count forecasts were not saved before the run. New estimates cannot reconstruct them.

metrics.label: Known main-run charge
metrics.note: Labels and evidence only; excludes unknown charges and other project work.

metrics.label: Calls with unknown charge
metrics.note: Unknown is not zero; reservations remain held.

metrics.label: Distinct review texts in the estimate
metrics.note: of 99,999 non-empty rows; duplicates reuse one label

rows.label: Labelling request time
rows.note: Estimate: serial. Measured: summed request time, not wall time.

The measured run covers 110,000 selected rows, not the first 100,000 rows of the file.
Charges are usage-derived and include every metered outcome. Uncertain calls carry no known charge. request_seconds is summed request time, not wall time.

items.title: Evidence extractor benchmark
items.question: Which hosted model extracts exact evidence quotes and product entities most reliably and cheaply?
items.sample: The same 100 development reviews selected for each route; DeepInfra attempted 100, Groq attempted 82.
items.truth: Exact-quote checks against the source text. Agreement with saved development evidence is in the report.

gaps.label: Attempt coverage incomplete
gaps.detail: 82 of 100 Groq reviews were attempted; 18 remain untouched. Invalid responses are observed failures, not missing attempts.

items.decision: DeepInfra became the evidence extractor: it completed more of the set with fewer invalid responses. Groq was faster per request.
limits: The benchmark stopped before Groq finished; its untouched reviews were never sent. request_seconds is summed request time, not wall time.
The paired comparison against development evidence is in reports/openrouter-extractor-benchmark.md.
Exact quotation is a structural check. Entity relevance and evidence quality lack human scoring.
Untouched reviews remain missing. Invalid responses remain measured failures; no new calls were made for this audit.

items.title: Blind verifier, ten reviews per request
items.question: Does an independent model, shown only the text and the rubric, give the same labels as Jev?
items.sample: 1000 accepted reviews from the main run, drawn by a fixed SHA-256 order; golden and pilot IDs excluded
items.truth: None. This is model-to-model agreement. It shows where two labellers differ, not which one is right.

metrics.label: Valid verifier outputs
metrics.note: 0 missing; model agreement on the selected sample.

metrics.label: Original verifier charge
metrics.note: Original run only; both follow-up runs are reported separately below.

items.finding: The completion run added 20 valid outputs. Combined coverage is 1000 of 1000; severity differs by 0.176 points on average. Original rejected outputs and unresolved holds remain saved.
limits: Agreement is not accuracy: both models can be wrong in the same way.
The verifier is gpt-oss-120b, the same base model as the evidence extractor, but with a separate prompt and no access to Jev's labels.

Combined agreement uses the original saved outputs plus the separate Crusoe completion run. Full sample coverage does not establish population accuracy. Original-run charges exclude the two separately reported follow-ups.

items.title: Jev with ten reviews per request
items.question: Does sending ten reviews in one Jev request change the labels or the cost?
items.sample: 100 reviews from the verifier sample, in 10 requests of 10
items.truth: None. Both sides are Jev with the same rubric; the reference is the main run's one-review requests.
items.finding: Jev reads the ten reviews once and answers forty questions, each pointed at one review. This sample used 16% fewer input tokens per review than the main-run average and differed on at least one label in 36 of 100 reviews, so the main run's one-review labels stay.
limits: Both sides are Jev jev-1.13.0 with rubric v2. Agreement measures how much batching moves the labels, not accuracy.
Jev's run-to-run variation on single reviews was not measured here, so part of the change may be ordinary variation.
The token comparison uses different sample populations; it does not isolate a causal batching saving.

items.title: Grouping as a recorded program stage
items.question: Does a saved, code-run grouping stage put reviews in the same issue as the historical agent handoff?
items.sample: 600 complaint and cancellation reviews from the historical issue map, blind to their issue
items.truth: The historical issue map. It was not validated by people, so disagreement is not proof of error.
items.finding: The original run saved 580 outputs; the first follow-up added ten and the completion run added 10. Combined coverage is 600 of 600. The historical 511/600 experiment remains separate; its unrecorded token usage is still unknown.
limits: The stage reads Jev's labels and evidence quote as context, as the historical grouping did.

items.title: Changed model claims and prompt injection
items.question: Do auditors flag changed model claims, and do synthetic instructions change model outputs?
items.sample: 100 of 100 label-auditor outputs (50 changed and 50 unchanged claims), 100 issue-auditor outputs, and the unchanged eight synthetic attack pairs
items.truth: Code altered saved model claims. These changes are not human-validated errors. Synthetic texts are excluded from all business results.

metrics.label: Paired label or issue changes
metrics.note: Jev, verifier and grouping on eight synthetic attack pairs

rows.label: Blind verifier disagreed with a changed label
Blind grouping disagreed with a changed issue
Auditor flagged an unchanged Jev label
Auditor flagged an unchanged historical issue

limits: Unchanged labels are Jev's and unchanged issues are historical; a flag on them is a disagreement, not proof of a false alarm.
Synthetic texts written for this test; excluded from all business results and accuracy figures. A changed label can be legitimate when the added sentence changes the review's meaning.
The historical target-reached helper does not cover every format, identity or canary attack. Paired label/issue changes are reported separately.
In the mixed-batch probe, verifier and grouping each changed one of eight benign rows; neither changed to the attacker value. These probes do not prove general injection resistance.

The separate OpenRouter/Crusoe follow-up added ten label-auditor outputs. Paired comparisons require both saved auditor and blind outputs. Flags on unchanged machine claims are disagreements, not proven false positives.
Before the follow-up, 41 of 50 selected changed-label cases had both outputs (41 of the 43 observed auditor cases). The new aggregate uses all 50 selected cases as its coverage denominator.
The completion run fills the remaining blind-output gaps. The auditor and synthetic injection results did not change.

items.title: 100-review pilot: cold and full warm replay
items.question: What did the full pilot cost, and can all six stages reuse saved outputs?
items.truth: Saved pilot receipts and a new offline execute() replay on a database copy. Source and before/after hashes match.

metrics.label: New paid / transport / socket attempts
metrics.note: All three counters are zero; all six stages executed.

limits: This separate pilot does not restore missing checkpoints or usage from the historical main run.
Warm stages reused cached model outputs; ranking was recomputed. No fresh inference or quality scoring occurred.
Two quarantines remain. Timing describes this local replay, not production latency or a scaling estimate.

items.sample: 337 attempts for 213 logical requests in the separate verification and robustness experiments. The separate follow-up used 10 attempts for five missing batches; its charges are shown separately. The completion run used 3 additional attempts under its separate USD0.33 allowance.
items.truth: Recomputed from public text-free call logs. Unknown charges retain their full reservation.

gaps.label: Billing unresolved
gaps.detail: 125 attempts have unknown charges; all reservations remain held. 1 of 213 logical requests have no settled result.

gaps.label: Follow-up billing unresolved
gaps.detail: 6 additional HTTP 429 attempts retain full reservations. All ten approved attempts are exhausted; old holds remain unchanged.

metrics.label: Settled requests resent after restart
metrics.note: 3 logical requests settled in the initial segment.

items.finding: 212 of 213 logical requests have a settled result; 1 has none. Retry attempts and unresolved holds are counted separately.
limits: Provider reconciliation is still needed for every unknown charge; HTTP errors are not assumed free.
Public logs support the phase and request arithmetic. SIGINT and checkpoint details remain saved-report evidence; private snapshots were not rechecked in this audit.
Public call rows omit provider-route and request/response receipt fields. This run does not prove historical main-run recovery.
The follow-up's USD0.38 allowance is separate. Its six shared-pool rate-limit responses and two invalid-ID responses remain recorded. No additional calls or released holds are implied.
Completion-run charges are shown separately. All original and first-follow-up holds remain; no historical charge was reconciled by the completion run.
